summary: Dependency-confusion probe against Wix thunderbolt with host-reconnaissance exfiltration to webhook.site
details: math-helpers-extra-utils@1.0.0 is advertised as 'Extra math helper utilities' and ships an empty index.js, but also includes thunderboltRegistry.js which registers factories under Wix-internal registry names (thunderboltRegistry, siteAssetsRegistry, editorRegistry, corvidRegistry, dataBindingRegistry, thunderboltBuilderRegistry, thunderboltPreviewRegistry) and a manifest referencing https://static.parastorage.com/unpkg/math-helpers-extra-utils@1.0.0/. When loaded via Wix's dynamic registry loader, a top-level IIFE in thunderboltRegistry.js executes child_process.execSync for `id`, `hostname`, and `uname -a`, collects platform, pid, and Node version, and issues a GET with those fields to the hardcoded third-party collector https://webhook.site/0492a36c-4d7b-408a-865c-226db25987ba. The declared package name is unrelated to Wix thunderbolt, and the registry-name hijack is the mechanism by which the exfiltration payload is reached — a dependency-confusion shape targeting Wix's internal build pipeline, with host reconnaissance of the building environment sent off-host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
